en: The Apadāna of the Elder Sattapāṭaliya Chapter on Praise (Thomakavagga) 5 The Apadāna of the Elder Sattapāṭaliya: In the past, when the lifespan was twenty thousand years, I was born as a human being in the world of men. At that time, there appeared in the world a Buddha, the Teacher named Padumuttara, the Great Sage. Having gone forth under that Blessed One, I practiced the holy life with diligence. I then made a vow before the Teacher: "May I become a disciple of the Victorious One. When the Teacher, the Lord of the World, had passed away into Nibbāna, his disciples, having gathered together, established a stūpa for the Tathāgata. It was seven *pāṭali* trees in height, and it shone like a mountain peak. I then offered a garland of flowers to that stūpa of the Great Sage. Because of that meritorious deed, for ninety-one eons I never fell into the lower realms, but always dwelt in the heavenly worlds. In my final existence, I was born in the city of Sāvatthī. There I saw the Teacher, the Buddha, the Exalted One, the Great Sage. Having seen the Teacher, the Conqueror, I went forth into homelessness. Through the power of that former vow, I attained the state of an Arhat. With a mind free from defilements, I have reached the end of suffering. I have fulfilled my task; there is no further birth for me. Thus did the Elder Sattapāṭaliya, having attained the fruit of Arhatship, recollect his own past deeds and speak them in the midst of the Saṅgha.
“Seated amidst the mountains, shining like a *kaṇikāra* flower,
I offered it to the Buddha.
I do not know a state of misery;
this is the fruit of worshipping the Buddha.
the Buddha's teaching has been accomplished.
Thus indeed did the venerable elder Sattapāṭaliya speak these verses.
The legend of the Elder Sattapāṭaliya is the fifth.
